items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: Leon Wright was a fine showman and Bill Evans, they were my two tenor men, Bill Evans and Leon Wright

ctx.x: That was one thing that I learned when I was first starting from T. Holder. If you're in there, you're not all that much better than the person you're sitting beside of and I guess when the men knew that that was the way I was, I guess they stood by me.

I heard you had a very colorful fellow, you did tell the most interesting story about Leon Wright taking the picture. Leon Wright was a fine showman and Bill Evans, they were my two tenor men, Bill Evans and Leon Wright and he would put on such a show, you'd have a battle of the saxes sometimes and poor Leon, compared with what Bill Evans played, was plain nothing, but he would steal the show from him everytime, and we would say Mr. Public
and Leon would do something (inaudible). As I said, I went for the jazz but I was going to put on something that I think would help bring the people in.
